mainTopic: Preparing מוקצה items for שבת use (fleece, palm branches, earth): designation, intention, action, or prior use, and the related dispute about דבר שאין מתכוין.
overview: This amud is about how an item that would normally be מוקצה can be made usable on שבת. It opens by finishing a challenge to רבא from the משנה about wool fleece used to insulate food. The גמרא gives two answers to that challenge. The first rewrites רבא's statement so that only fleece designated for insulating may be moved. The second is רבינא's: the משנה is talking about a merchant's fleece. A ברייתא about palm branches cut for firewood follows, where the תנא קמא requires tying them and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל does not. On that ברייתא, רב requires tying, שמואל says intention is enough, and רב אסי says sitting on them before שבת is enough, and sources from the תנאים are found to back רב אסי. The unnamed תנא is identified as רבי חנינא בן עקיבא. Then רב יהודה permits earth brought into a set corner of the house, and רב פפא explains that even the רבנן do not require an action where none is possible. Finally, the גמרא compares two ברייתות about polishing with sand, explains them through the dispute about דבר שאין מתכוין, and begins a challenge that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the challenge: the fleece must fall by itself
steps.stepSummary: The challenge against רבא finishes: the משנה says you lift the cover and the fleece falls on its own, which shows the fleece itself may not be moved.
steps.simpleTranslation: He lifts the cover, and the fleece falls by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes the challenge against רבא, quoting the משנה. It shows that even fleece used for insulating may not be moved by hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא had said that fleece used to insulate food may be moved. The משנה forces a roundabout method instead: lift the cover, which may be moved, and let the fleece drop. If moving the fleece were allowed, this method would be pointless, so רבא seems to be contradicted.

keyTerms.meaning: the cover or lid over the pot, which may be moved
they fall (the fleece slides off by itself)
wool fleece, the material used for insulating

steps.confusionAlert: This amud begins in the middle of the challenge. The words 'he lifts the cover' are the משנה's answer to the question 'how does he get the pot out?' They are being used here as an attack on רבא. They are not a new ruling.

phrases.english: He lifts the cover,
phrases.notes: The cover may be moved.

phrases.english: and they (the fleece) fall by themselves.
phrases.notes: So the fleece is never moved directly by hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: נוֹטֵל אֶת הַכִּיסּוּי וְהֵן נוֹפְלוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge from the משנה against רבא's statement, which came on the previous amud.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's statement that fleece used for insulating may be moved on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה requires an indirect method (lifting the cover). That only makes sense if the fleece itself is מוקצה even after it was used for insulating.

steps.title: רבא's statement restated: only fleece designated for insulating may be moved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rewrites what רבא said: the משנה's ban applies only to fleece not designated for insulating. Fleece designated for insulating may be moved.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said: רבא said, 'They only taught this when he did not designate the fleece for insulating. But if he designated it for insulating, it may be moved.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by changing the version of רבא's statement. רבא was not arguing with the משנה. He was limiting it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the old version, using the fleece once was enough to permit moving it, and the משנה contradicted that. In the new version, רבא explains the משנה: its ban covers fleece that was used for insulating without being set aside for that purpose. Only fleece he deliberately designated for insulating loses its מוקצה status.

keyTerms.meaning: if it was said, this is how it was said (a corrected version of a statement)
they taught this only in the case of (limits the scope of a ruling)
he designated them, set them aside for a purpose
insulating food to keep it hot
one may move them (not מוקצה)

steps.whatToRemember: Simply using fleece to insulate is not enough. It must be designated (ייחוד) for insulating for it to be movable.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not disagreeing with the משנה. The rewritten statement explains the משנה. The משנה's case is fleece that was NOT designated.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was stated, it was stated like this:
phrases.notes: Formula introducing a corrected version.

phrases.english: Rava said:
They taught this only
phrases.notes: Refers to the משנה's ban on moving the fleece.

phrases.english: where he did not designate them for insulating.
But if he designated them for insulating —
one may move them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי אִיתְּמַר הָכִי אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1 by rewriting רבא's statement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Corrected version of the statement (rewording), which limits the משנה to undesignated fleece.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא permitted moving any fleece that was used for insulating, which contradicts the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה bans moving undesignated fleece. Fleece designated for insulating may be moved.

steps.title: Support from רבין's tradition in the name of רבי
steps.stepSummary: A tradition brought by רבין in the name of רבי says exactly the same as רבא's revised statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: when רבין came, he said that רבי יעקב said that רבי אסי בן שאול said that רבי said: 'They only taught this when he did not designate the fleece for insulating. But if he designated it, it may be moved.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports the revised version of רבא with an identical teaching from ארץ ישראל, going back to רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording matches the revised רבא word for word. This shows the rule about designation is an old, established tradition. It also strengthens the claim that the revised version is the correct one.

keyTerms.meaning: it was also stated (a supporting אמוראic teaching)
when רבין came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)

phrases.english: It was also stated:
When Ravin came, he said

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי בֶּן שָׁאוּל
phrases.english: that Rabbi Ya'akov said that Rabbi Asi ben Shaul said
that Rabbi (Yehuda HaNasi) said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא יִחֲדָן לְהַטְמָנָה,
phrases.english: They taught this only where he did not designate them for insulating,
but if he designated them for insulating —
one may move them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר נָמֵי כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the revised version of רבא in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: The revised version of רבא: designated fleece may be moved, and undesignated fleece may not.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבין's tradition in the name of רבי, through רבי יעקב and רבי אסי בן שאול.

steps.title: רבינא: the משנה speaks of a merchant's fleece
steps.stepSummary: רבינא gives a different answer. He keeps רבא's original statement and explains that the משנה is about fleece from a merchant's stock.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא says: They taught the משנה about fleece from the merchant's shelves.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא offers a second way out of the challenge without changing רבא's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבינא, using fleece for insulating normally does make it movable, as רבא first said. The משנה's ban is about merchandise (הפתק) kept for sale. The owner still cares about it as stock, so it stays מוקצה even after it was used for insulating.

keyTerms.meaning: a merchant's shelves or stock, where goods are kept for sale
they taught this about fleece from the merchant's stock

steps.confusionAlert: רבינא does not accept the revised version from step 2. This is a separate, alternative answer that keeps רבא's original statement.

phrases.english: Ravina says:
They taught it about fleece from the merchant's shelves.
phrases.notes: The משנה's ban is limited to merchandise.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא אוֹמֵר בְּשֶׁל הֶפְתֵּק שָׁנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An alternative answer to the challenge in step 1, different from the rewording in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case of the משנה (אוקימתא) to merchant's fleece.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to ban moving any fleece used for insulating.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only merchant's fleece set aside for sale is banned. Ordinary fleece used for insulating may be moved, as רבא originally said.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבינא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that merchant's fleece may not be moved, but if a homeowner prepared it for use, it may be moved.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught in a ברייתא: Fleece from the merchant's shelves may not be moved. But if a homeowner prepared it for his own use, it may be moved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that matches רבינא's distinction exactly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא names merchant's fleece (הפתק) as the case that may not be moved. It contrasts that with fleece a homeowner prepared for use, which may be moved. This confirms that the משנה's ban fits the merchant's case.

keyTerms.meaning: it was also taught this way (support from a ברייתא)
he prepared them (for use)
a homeowner, as opposed to a merchant

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to the challenge against רבא. (1) The rewording: only fleece designated for insulating may be moved. (2) רבינא: the משנה is about merchant's fleece, and a ברייתא supports him.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a basic idea in מוקצה: whether an item may be moved depends on what the owner has in mind for it, such as keeping it as stock or preparing it for use.

phrases.english: It was also taught so (in a baraita):
Wool fleece from the merchant's shelves
may not be moved.
But if the homeowner prepared them
to use them —
one may move them.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבינא's answer in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: רבינא's claim that the משנה's ban refers to merchant's fleece.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא distinguishing merchant's fleece (may not be moved) from fleece a homeowner prepared for use (may be moved).

steps.title: Palm branches cut for firewood, then set aside for sitting
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה teaches a ברייתא before רב. If palm branches were cut for wood and the owner then decided to sit on them, the תנא קמא says he must tie them together. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says tying is not needed. רבה בר בר חנה rules like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה taught before רב: palm branches that someone cut for firewood, and then he changed his mind and wanted them for sitting, need to be tied together. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says they do not need to be tied. He taught it, and he also said: the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא on the same theme we have been learning. The theme is how an item meant for one use can be made usable on שבת for a different use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Branches cut for firewood are מוקצה, because firewood may not be moved on שבת. The question is what makes them count as 'seats' instead. The תנא קמא requires a physical act, tying them, while רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says this act is not needed, and the הלכה follows him.

keyTerms.meaning: Hard palm branches
He cut them off the tree
He changed his mind / reconsidered
To tie them together, which turns them into a usable seat
The practical ruling follows this opinion

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the base for the whole מחלוקת of רב, שמואל, and רב אסי that follows.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חַנָּה קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana taught before Rav:
Hard palm branches that one cut for firewood,
and he reconsidered them for sitting —
he must tie them together.
phrases.notes: Tying is done before שבת.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
He does not need to tie them.

phrases.aramaic: הוּא תָּנֵי לַהּ וְהוּא אָמַר לַהּ:
phrases.english: He taught it, and he said about it:
phrases.notes: רבה בר בר חנה himself.

phrases.english: The halakha follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חַנָּה קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from designating fleece to a related case of re-designating palm branches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא says palm branches cut for firewood need tying to be usable as seats. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says they do not, and the הלכה follows him.

steps.title: Three אמוראים: tie, intend, or sit
steps.stepSummary: רב says one must tie the branches. שמואל says it is enough to intend to sit on them. רב אסי says it is enough to sit on them before שבת, even without tying and even without intending.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said: רב says he ties them. שמואל says he has them in mind. רב אסי says he sits on them, even if he did not tie them and even if he did not have them in mind.
steps.whatsHappening: Three אמוראים argue about what a person must do before שבת to make these branches usable as seats.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three levels. רב requires a physical change (tying). שמואל requires only a thought (מחשבה). רב אסי says actual use before שבת works even with no tying and no thought.

keyTerms.meaning: It was said, which introduces a dispute among אמוראים
He ties
He intends / has in mind
He sits on them before שבת

steps.confusionAlert: רב אסי's position is not just a third way of designating. He says sitting works even without any thought at all, so actual use is enough by itself.

phrases.english: It was stated: Rav said: He ties,
and Shmuel said: He has it in mind,
and Rav Asi said: He sits,
even though he did not tie
and even though he did not have it in mind.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר רַב אָמַר: קוֹשֵׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the אמוראים' positions on the case in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: tying is required. שמואל: intention is enough. רב אסי: sitting on them before שבת is enough, even without tying or intention.

steps.title: Whose view does רב אסי follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רב matches the תנא קמא and שמואל matches רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. But רב אסי seems to match neither תנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that רב said his view like the תנא קמא. And שמואל also said his view like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. But רב אסי, whose view does he follow?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אסי. An אמורא normally needs a תנא to back him up, and it looks like he has none.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only shows two options: tying (תנא קמא) or not tying, which means just thinking (רבן שמעון בן גמליאל). רב אסי permits even with no thought at all, so he seems to go against both תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense that... (sets up a contrast)
The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה or ברייתא
Like whom? Whose opinion does he follow?

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא רַב הוּא דְּאָמַר כְּתַנָּא קַמָּא,
phrases.english: Granted, Rav stated his view like the first tanna,
and Shmuel too stated his view
like Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.
But Rav Asi, like whom did he state his view?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא רַב הוּא דְּאָמַר כְּתַנָּא קַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Matches each אמורא to a תנא from the ברייתא and finds רב אסי unsupported.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's ruling that sitting alone is enough
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Neither opinion in the ברייתא permits the branches without tying or thought, so רב אסי seems to have no תנא behind him.

steps.title: רב אסי follows the תנא of the bandages
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי follows a different תנא, who teaches that wearing bandages outside for a short time before שבת permits going out with them on שבת. This is true even if they were not prepared in the usual way.
steps.simpleTranslation: He follows this תנא, as it was taught: You may go out on שבת with bandages of combed flax or wool when you dipped them in oil and tied them on with string. If you did not dip them in oil and did not tie them with string, you may not go out with them. But if you went out with them for a short time while it was still day, before שבת, then even though you did not dip them or tie them with string, you may go out with them on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by finding a different תנא who agrees with רב אסי. This תנא holds that using an item before שבת is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the bandages need preparation, oil and tying, to count as part of the wound dressing. This תנא says that simply wearing them before שבת replaces that preparation. In the same way, sitting on the branches before שבת replaces tying or intending.

keyTerms.meaning: Combed flax used as a bandage
Combed wool
Dipped them in oil
Twine / string
While it is still day, before שבת

steps.whatToRemember: There are three ways to make palm branches usable as seats: tying (רב / תנא קמא), intending (שמואל / רבן שמעון בן גמליאל), and actual use before שבת (רב אסי / the תנא of the bandages).
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that actual use before שבת can work like formal preparation, and this idea has a source among the תנאים.

phrases.aramaic: הוּא דְּאָמַר כִּי הַאי תַּנָּא דְּתַנְיָא:
phrases.english: He stated his view like this tanna, as it was taught:
One may go out with combed flax and combed wool,
when he dipped them in oil
and tied them with twine.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא צְבָעָן בְּשֶׁמֶן וְלֹא כְּרָכָן בִּמְשִׁיחָה —
phrases.english: If he did not dip them in oil and did not tie them with twine —
one may not go out with them.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם יָצָא בָּהֶן שָׁעָה אַחַת מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם,
phrases.english: And if he went out with them for a short time while it was still day,
even though he did not dip them
and did not tie them with twine,
he is permitted to go out with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא דְּאָמַר כִּי הַאי תַּנָּא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by bringing a תנא who supports רב אסי.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב אסי has no תנא supporting him.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא of the bandages holds that use before שבת works even without the usual preparation, which supports רב אסי.

steps.title: A משנה about straw on a bed supports רב אסי
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי brings a משנה showing that straw becomes usable on שבת if a pillow or sheet was spread on it before שבת. This supports רב אסי's view that brief use before שבת is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: We also learned this in a משנה. Straw lying on a bed may not be moved with one's hand, but he may move it with his body. But if it was animal food, or if a pillow or sheet was on it while it was still day before שבת, he may move it with his hand. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings extra support for רב אסי from a משנה. It shows that simply using the straw before שבת (lying on it with a sheet) makes it usable on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Straw on a bed is normally set aside for fuel or building, so it is מוקצה and cannot be moved by hand. But if someone used it for lying on before שבת, by putting a pillow or sheet on it, that use is enough to change its status. No tying or special act is needed, which is exactly what רב אסי said about the branches.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned it (in a משנה): a formula bringing support from a tannaitic source
Straw
Moves it with his body, an unusual way of moving that is allowed even for מוקצה
While it was still day, meaning before שבת began
Learn from this: the proof is accepted

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי, אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: We too have also learned:
Straw that is on top of the bed
phrases.notes: The straw is meant for fuel or building, so it is מוקצה.

phrases.english: he may not move it with his hand,
but he may move it with his body.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אִם הָיָה עָלָיו מַאֲכַל בְּהֵמָה,
phrases.english: But if it was designated as animal food,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁהָיָה עָלָיו כַּר אוֹ סָדִין מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם —
phrases.english: or if there was a pillow or sheet on it while it was still day,
phrases.notes: He lay on it before שבת. This is the brief use that matters.

phrases.english: he may move it with his hand.
Conclude from it.
phrases.notes: There is a tannaitic source matching רב אסי.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי, אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second tannaitic source to the answer in Step 9 that רב אסי has a תנא behind him.
steps.raayaObject: רב אסי's view that brief use before שבת removes מוקצה status without tying or intent
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about straw on a bed with a pillow or sheet spread on it before שבת

steps.title: Who is the תנא who argues with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the identity of the unnamed תנא קמא who requires tying the palm branches.
steps.simpleTranslation: And who is the תנא who disagrees with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the palm-branch ברייתא and asks who the unnamed first opinion is. This sets up the next step, which gives a name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 6 the תנא קמא required tying and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל did not. The גמרא now wants to know which named sage held the stricter view.

keyTerms.meaning: And who is the תנא, a question asking to identify an unnamed opinion
Who disagrees with him

phrases.english: And who is the tanna who disagrees with
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel?
phrases.notes: Meaning the תנא קמא who required tying the branches.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן תְּנָא דִּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רב אסי discussion and returns to the ברייתא of Step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the unnamed תנא קמא who requires tying

steps.title: It is רבי חנינא בן עקיבא, with the story of the palm branches
steps.stepSummary: The answer is רבי חנינא בן עקיבא. The גמרא tells a story where he told his students to have in mind to sit on cut palm branches, and זעירי was not sure if it was a wedding house or a mourning house.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי חנינא בן עקיבא. When רב דימי came, he said that זעירי said that רבי חנינא said: Once רבי חנינא בן עקיבא went to a place and found palm branches that had been cut for firewood. He said to his students: Go out and have in mind that we will sit on them tomorrow. And I do not know whether it was a wedding feast house or a house of mourning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names רבי חנינא בן עקיבא as the תנא who requires tying. It tells a story about him to back this up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first the story seems to say the opposite, because he only asked his students to think about sitting on the branches and did not ask them to tie them. The detail that זעירי did not know whether it was a wedding or a mourning house becomes the key to solving this in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: When רב דימי came from ארץ ישראל to בבל, a common way of introducing a teaching
Hard palm branches
Have in mind, form an intention
House of a wedding feast
House of mourning

steps.confusionAlert: Do not be thrown off: this story looks like it supports needing only thought, like שמואל. The next step explains why רבי חנינא בן עקיבא still generally requires tying.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Ḥanina ben Akiva.
As when Rav Dimi came,
he said that Ze'iri said that Rabbi Ḥanina said:

phrases.aramaic: פַּעַם אַחַת הָלַךְ רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן עֲקִיבָא לְמָקוֹם אֶחָד,
phrases.english: Once Rabbi Ḥanina ben Akiva went to a certain place,
and found hard palm branches
that they had cut for wood,
phrases.notes: Meaning firewood, so they were set aside and מוקצה.

phrases.english: and he said to his students:
Go out and have in mind
so that we may sit on them tomorrow.
phrases.notes: Tomorrow means on שבת.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא יָדַעְנָא אִי בֵּית הַמִּשְׁתֶּה הֲוָה,
phrases.english: And I do not know whether it was a house of a feast,
phrases.notes: These are זעירי's words.

phrases.english: or whether it was a house of mourning.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן עֲקִיבָא. דְּכִי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תנא קמא is רבי חנינא בן עקיבא, shown through a story about palm branches

steps.title: Thought was enough only because a busy household could not tie
steps.stepSummary: Since זעירי's doubt was only between a wedding house and a mourning house, the leniency applied only to busy situations. Normally רבי חנינא בן עקיבא requires tying.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the fact that he said, 'whether it was a wedding feast house or a mourning house,' we learn that only at a mourning house or a feast house, where people are busy, is thought enough. But here, in a normal case, if he tied them, yes; if he did not tie them, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the story does not contradict the claim that רבי חנינא בן עקיבא requires tying. Intent was enough only because the people there were too busy to tie.
steps.deeperAnalysis: זעירי was only unsure which of the two busy kinds of houses it was, so he was sure it was a busy setting. That shows the leniency of thought alone was a special exception for busy households. In an ordinary case, the rule stays that the branches must be tied, matching the תנא קמא.

keyTerms.meaning: From the fact that he said, introducing an inference from the wording
Specifically, only in this case
They are busy or preoccupied
He tied

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא who requires tying is רבי חנינא בן עקיבא. His story where thought alone was enough applied only at a busy wedding or mourning house. Normally, tying is required.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how a story that looks like it goes against a ruling can actually be a special exception under that ruling, because of the unusual setting.

phrases.english: From the fact that he said: whether it was a house of a feast
or whether it was a house of mourning,

phrases.aramaic: דַּוְקָא בֵּית הָאֵבֶל אוֹ בֵּית הַמִּשְׁתֶּה
phrases.english: it is specifically a house of mourning or a house of a feast
because they are busy,
phrases.notes: They have no time to tie the branches, so intent is enough.

phrases.english: but here, in a normal case, if he tied them, yes,
if he did not tie them, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּקָאָמַר אִי בֵּית הַמִּשְׁתֶּה הֲוָה אִי בֵּית הָאֵבֶל הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the hidden difficulty that the story in Step 12 seems to require only intent.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the story to a special case (busy household)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The story shows רבי חנינא בן עקיבא holds that thought alone is enough, so he cannot be the תנא who requires tying.
steps.terutzMaskana: Thought alone was enough only because a wedding or mourning house is too busy to tie. In normal cases he requires tying, matching the תנא קמא.

steps.title: Bringing a basket of earth into the house for שבת use
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that a person may bring a full basket of earth into the house before שבת and use it for all his needs on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: A person may bring in a full basket of earth and use it for all his needs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling about another item that could be מוקצה: earth. Bringing it into the house before שבת prepares it for use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earth is normally מוקצה because it is not a usable item. By bringing it inside before שבת for household uses, like covering excrement, he shows it is prepared, so it may be used on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Brings in
Basket
Earth, dirt
All his needs

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
A person may bring in a full basket of earth,
phrases.notes: He does this before שבת.

phrases.english: and use it for all his needs.
phrases.notes: For example, covering excrement on שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: מַכְנִיס אָדָם מְלֹא קוּפָּתוֹ עָפָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case in the same theme of preparing items before שבת so they are not מוקצה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Earth brought into the house before שבת may be used for all one's needs on שבת.

steps.title: The earth must have a set corner
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא, in the name of מר זוטרא רבה, limits רב יהודה's ruling: it applies only if he set aside a corner of the house for the earth.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא taught in the name of מר זוטרא רבה: This is only if he designated a corner for it.
steps.whatsHappening: A later sage adds a condition to רב יהודה's ruling. The earth counts as prepared only if it is placed in a specific corner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the earth is just spread all over the floor, it looks like part of the ground and not a prepared item. Setting aside a corner shows it is being kept for use, so it is not מוקצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught publicly, expounded
In the name of
And that is only when, a formula adding a condition
A corner

phrases.english: Mar Zutra taught
in the name of Mar Zutra the Great:
That is only if he designated a corner for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ מָר זוּטְרָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּמָר זוּטְרָא רַבָּה: וְהוּא שֶׁיִּחֵד לוֹ קֶרֶן זָוִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limiting condition to רב יהודה's ruling in Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The earth is permitted only if a specific corner of the house was set aside for it.

steps.title: Does the earth ruling only follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים suggest to רב פפא that the earth ruling must follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, because the רבנן require a physical action.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages said before רב פפא: Whose view is this? It must be רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's. Because if it followed the רבנן, they say we need an action.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים ask whose opinion the earth ruling follows. They suggest it can only fit רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who holds that thought alone is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the ruling, simply setting aside a corner for the earth is enough. That is preparation by thought and designation alone. The רבנן (the unnamed תנא קמא of the palm branches) required tying them, which is a physical action. So the ruling seems to clash with the majority view.

keyTerms.meaning: Like whom? Whose opinion does this follow?
The תנא who holds that intention alone is enough to prepare palm branches
We require a physical action (to prepare an item for שבת)
The Sages, meaning the majority view

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'רבנן' in 'כרבנן' means the תנא קמא of the palm-branch dispute, who required tying. It does not mean the Sages who are speaking to רב פפא.

phrases.english: The Sages said before Rav Pappa:
In accordance with whom? In accordance with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.
For if it were in accordance with the Rabbis,
don't they say we require an action?
phrases.notes: For example, tying the palm branches together.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ רַבָּנַן קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא: כְּמַאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the ruling of מר זוטרא from Step 15 against the palm-branch dispute from Steps 11–13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא does the 'designated corner' ruling follow? Does it contradict the רבנן?
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that designating a corner is enough (Step 15)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רבנן require a physical action. Designating a corner is not an action. So the ruling would only fit the minority view of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.title: רב פפא: An action is only required when one is possible
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that the רבנן only require an action for items on which an action can be done. Earth is not such an item.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to them: You can even say it follows the רבנן. The רבנן only said we need an action for something you can do an action with. But for something you cannot do an action with, they did not say so.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא defends the ruling. He shows it can fit the majority view of the רבנן too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Palm branches can be tied, so the רבנן demand that action. Earth is just loose dirt, and there is no meaningful action you can do to it. So for earth, even the רבנן accept designation alone. This limits the רבנן's rule to cases where an action is possible.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say (the ruling can fit even this view)
They only said their ruling up to this point (a limiting formula)
Something on which it is possible to do an action

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב פפא, the רבנן's demand for a מעשה only applies where an action is possible. Where no action is possible, designation alone works for everyone.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to them:
You can even say it follows the Rabbis.
The Rabbis only said
that we require an action

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מִידֵּי דְּבַר מֶיעְבַּד בֵּיהּ מַעֲשֶׂה,
phrases.english: for something on which it is possible to do an action.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מִידֵּי דְּלָא בַּר מֶיעְבַּד בֵּיהּ מַעֲשֶׂה — לָא.
phrases.english: But for something on which it is not possible to do an action, they did not say so.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב פָּפָּא: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 16 by narrowing the scope of the רבנן's requirement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope (אוקימתא of the רבנן's rule to items on which an action is possible)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן require an action for every set-aside item, so the earth ruling contradicts them.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן require an action only where one is possible. Earth cannot be acted upon, so designation is enough even for them.

steps.title: Suggesting a tannaitic parallel: polishing utensils
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that the same question is an older argument between תנאים. It cites a ברייתא implying that polishing with נתר and sand is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is like an argument between תנאים? A ברייתא teaches: One may polish utensils with anything, except silver utensils with גרתקון. This implies that נתר and sand are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that the 'action or no action' question was already argued by תנאים. It brings the first source, which permits sand. This sets up the contradicting source that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sand is like earth: you cannot do a meaningful preparing action with it. The ברייתא implies that you may use נתר and sand on שבת. That would fit the view that no action is required. The גמרא is building toward a contrast with a second source.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say this is like a dispute between תנאים?
Scrub or polish
A strong polishing agent (cream of tartar) that also smooths silver
Natron (a cleaning mineral) and sand

steps.confusionAlert: Silver with גרתקון is forbidden because it smooths the metal, which is close to a מלאכה. That exception is about a different issue, not about whether an action is required.

phrases.english: Shall we say this is like a dispute between the Tannaim?
With anything one may polish utensils,
except for silver utensils with cream of tartar.
This implies that natron and sand are permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: נֵימָא כְּתַנָּאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רב פפא's defense to searching for an earlier תנאים dispute on the same question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the need for a מעשה with items like earth or sand already argued by תנאים?

steps.title: Contradicting source: sand is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא forbids נתר and sand. The גמרא suggests the two sources argue over whether an action is required.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: נתר and sand are forbidden. Isn't it that they argue about this? One Sage holds we require an action, and the other holds we do not require an action.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source that forbids sand. It suggests that the two ברייתות disagree exactly on whether a physical action is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The forbidding view would hold that an action is required. Since nothing can be done to sand, it stays forbidden. The permitting view would hold that no action is required. If this reading is right, the forbidding תנא disagrees with רב פפא's claim that everyone permits items on which no action is possible.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught (introducing a contradicting ברייתא)
Isn't it that? (proposing an explanation)
They argue
One Sage holds

steps.whyThisMatters: If the dispute really is about requiring a מעשה, then רב פפא's distinction is not shared by all תנאים. The earth ruling would then depend on taking one side.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: Natron and sand are prohibited?
Isn't it that they argue about this:
that one Sage holds we require an action,
and the other Sage holds we do not require an action.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: נֶתֶר וָחוֹל — אָסוּר. מַאי לָאו בְּהָא קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the 'נימא כתנאי' suggestion begun in Step 18 by bringing the opposing source and naming the proposed point of dispute.
steps.raayaObject: That whether a מעשה is required for items like sand or earth is a dispute between תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: Two ברייתות: one implies נתר and sand are permitted, the other says they are forbidden

steps.title: No, the two sources argue about something else
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that the two ברייתות argue about requiring an action. Everyone agrees no action is needed. One ברייתא follows רבי יהודה and the other follows רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone agrees we do not need an action. And there is no contradiction: this ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, and that ברייתא follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own suggestion from the last step. It says the two ברייתות do not argue about needing an action. They are explained by a different, older argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 19 the גמרא proposed that the forbidding ברייתא requires an action and the permitting ברייתא does not. Now the גמרא says both agree that no action is needed. So the earlier argument between the חכמים and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is no longer tied to this תנאים debate. The contradiction will be solved by matching each ברייתא to a different תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
We do not require a physical action
And it is not difficult; there is no contradiction
This one... that one... (matching each source to a different opinion)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is now saying an action IS required. It is saying the opposite: everyone agrees no action is needed. The disagreement between the ברייתות comes from a completely different issue.

phrases.english: No, everyone agrees
that we do not require an action
and it is not difficult:

phrases.aramaic: הָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, הָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן.
phrases.english: this one follows Rabbi Yehuda, that one follows Rabbi Shimon.
phrases.notes: The forbidding ברייתא follows רבי יהודה. The permitting ברייתא follows רבי שמעון.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא בָּעֵינַן מַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proposal of Steps 18-19 and offers a different way to reconcile the two ברייתות.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the two ברייתות argue about whether an action is required.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The contradiction can be explained by a different, well-known תנאים debate, so it does not prove a dispute about requiring an action.

steps.title: The argument is about unintended results
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the new reading. רבי יהודה forbids an act whose forbidden result is unintended, so he forbids the sand and נתר. רבי שמעון permits it, so he allows them.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, who said that an unintended act is forbidden. That ברייתא follows רבי שמעון, who said that an unintended act is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out what it meant by 'this follows רבי יהודה, that follows רבי שמעון.' It ties each ברייתא to its opinion about unintended results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Polishing silver with sand or נתר also smooths the metal, which is forbidden on שבת, even though the person does not intend that. רבי יהודה holds that an unintended forbidden result still makes the act forbidden, so he forbids it. רבי שמעון holds that an unintended result is permitted, so he allows it.

keyTerms.meaning: An unintended act: a permitted action that may cause a forbidden result the person did not intend
Forbidden
Permitted

steps.whyThisMatters: The dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון about דבר שאין מתכוין is one of the most important principles in the laws of שבת. It comes up again and again throughout ש״ס.

phrases.english: This one follows Rabbi Yehuda, who said:
an unintended act is forbidden.
phrases.notes: So polishing with sand, which smooths the metal without intending to, is forbidden.

phrases.english: That one follows Rabbi Shimon, who said:
an unintended act is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, דְּאָמַר: דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין מִתְכַּוֵּין — אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the short answer of Step 20 and explains the reasoning behind each side.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns each ברייתא to a different תנא based on the principle of דבר שאין מתכוין.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתות argue about whether an action is required to set an item aside for שבת use.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתות argue about דבר שאין מתכוין. רבי יהודה forbids and רבי שמעון permits.

steps.title: But the permitting source forbids washing hair
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new reading. The permitting ברייתא's last clause forbids washing hair with these substances. רבי שמעון would allow even that, so the ברייתא cannot follow him. The גמרא begins to quote a משנה to prove this.
steps.simpleTranslation: How did you explain the ברייתא that permits? As following רבי שמעון. But look at the end of that same ברייתא: 'However, one may not wash his hair with them.' If it follows רבי שמעון, he permits that! As we learned in a משנה:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave by pointing to the last clause of the permitting ברייתא. It then opens a quote from a משנה. That משנה is the proof, and it will come at the start of the next passage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Washing hair with sand or נתר may pull out hairs, but the person does not intend that. For רבי שמעון, an unintended result is permitted, so he should allow washing hair. Since the ברייתא forbids it, the ברייתא does not seem to follow רבי שמעון. That undermines the answer from Steps 20-21.

keyTerms.meaning: How did you establish (explain) it?
Say (look at) the last clause
Wash (one's hair)
As we learned in a משנה (introduces a quote)

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase דִּתְנַן is only the doorway to the proof. The actual משנה that shows רבי שמעון permits washing hair is quoted at the start of the next passage.

phrases.english: How did you establish the one that permits?
As following Rabbi Shimon.
Say the last clause:
'However, one may not wash his hair with them.'
phrases.notes: Washing hair with these may pull out hair, which is an unintended result.

phrases.english: And if it is Rabbi Shimon, he does permit it!
As we learned in a mishna:
phrases.notes: Setup line. The משנה itself appears on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי אוֹקֵימְתָּא לְהָא דְּשָׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of Steps 20-21 that matches the permitting ברייתא to רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the permitting ברייתא follows רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same ברייתא forbids washing hair with sand or נתר. That is also an unintended result, which רבי שמעון permits. So the ברייתא contradicts רבי שמעון's view.
